# Sparkline  (@elabs-ai/components-charts)
import: import { Sparkline } from "@elabs-ai/components-charts";
story: https://elabs-ai.com/storybook/?path=/docs/charts-sparkline--docs
purpose: Tiny, axis-less trend that lives inside a KPI tile or a table cell.  [chart]
  used inside: MetricCard, DataTable
anti-patterns (avoid):
  x Adding axes and tooltips to a Sparkline — if it needs them it is a LineChart.
  x A Sparkline as the only carrier of a number — pair it with the value (MetricCard).
  x Fixing its width in pixels — let the tile or cell own the box so it reflows.
extends: Omit<
  SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>,
  "children" | "values" | "target"
>
props (own-declared):
  values: number[]  — The series, oldest → newest.
  variant?: "bar" | "line"  — Visual form. Default "bar".
  emphasizeLast?: boolean  — Emphasize the newest value with the `--chart-1` token. Default true for bars.
  label?: string  — Accessible name. Default describes the series (and any references below).
  width?: number  — Rendered size when `fit="fixed"` (default) — the SVG's actual pixel geometry, unaffected by any CSS box the caller gives it. Also the FALLBACK size for `fit="fill"` before the first real measurement lands.
  height?: number
  fit?: "fixed" | "fill"  — Sizing strategy. `"fixed"` (default) draws at exactly `width`×`height` — unchanged no matter what CSS box (`className="w-full"`, a table cell, …) the caller puts it in, exactly as before this prop existed. `"fill"` measures the real rendered width of that CSS box (a tiny, cleaned-up `ResizeObserver`, falling back to `width` before the first measurement or where `ResizeObserver` isn't available, e.g. jsdom) and draws the plot at that real pixel width instead — no CSS stretching, so line strokes, the emphasized dot and the last-value label never distort. Opt in per usage (a trend card, a scorecard cell) rather than globally, since most Sparkline call sites size it explicitly and shouldn't pay for a measurement round-trip.
  target?: number  — A horizontal reference line ("goal", "quota") drawn across the plot in `--chart-foreground-muted`, dashed — never recolours the series even when the latest value falls short; status is the card's job, not the sparkline's. The reference sits a rung BELOW the data it is read against (b-7): the series is promoted to `--chart-foreground` whenever any reference is drawn, so the measured thing is always the strongest mark on the plot.
  baseline?: number[]  — A comparison series (e.g. last year), same index alignment as `values`. Drawn as a thin `--chart-foreground-muted` line behind the main series, in both variants.
  band?: readonly [number, number]  — A "normal range" `[lo, hi]` drawn as a quiet filled zone behind everything.
  fitDomain?: boolean  — For `variant="line"` with no `target`/`baseline`/`band`: use the series' own min–max (padded) domain instead of the shared zero-based bar scale. A tight-range series (a weekly count moving ±5% around its own mean) reads as a flat line on a zero-based scale — decoration with no information (WCAG 1.4.1's "a channel that carries nothing" failure mode, not a colour one). Default false — byte-identical to today's shared scale when unset.
  showLastValue?: boolean  — Render the formatted latest value as text to the right of the plot. Default false.
  formatValue?: (value: number) => string  — Formats every value this component surfaces as text (the last-value label and the accessible name's numbers). Default: locale number formatting.
  lastValueSuffix?: string  — Appended (with a leading space) to the `showLastValue` text and to the accessible name's "latest …" phrase — e.g. `"this wk"` when the plotted series is weekly but a nearby headline figure is a different period (a quarter total), so the last-value label cannot be misread as the same fact at a different scale. Default: none (today's behaviour).
  labels?: SparklineLabels  — Words for the reference facts in the default accessible name.

args.shape: single value against a target threshold

content.text:
chart-for "single value against a target threshold" — 5 candidate(s), ranked:
  read as: measure
  1. Gauge  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 5)
     shape: a single value against a target or threshold bands
     avoid when: the trend over time matters more than the instant — use a line chart
  2. BulletChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 4)
     shape: a single value against a target and 2–3 qualitative bands
     avoid when: more than one value/target pair needs comparing — use a small-multiple row of bullets or a `DumbbellChart`
  3. RingChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 2)
     shape: one proportion against its maximum, read as a single ring
     avoid when: several categories matter — use a pie or unit chart
  4. BarChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 2)
     shape: a single signed measure around a meaningful zero, as diverging bars with a zero line
     avoid when: a time axis with many points — use a line or area chart
  5. ChoroplethChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 1)
     shape: a measure by geographic region
     avoid when: there is no real geography — use a bar chart

also consider (props, not other charts):
  + analytics={[{ kind: "line", value: "mean" }]} — a computed reference line (a number for a fixed target)

Per the chart-selection rules: compare at least 3 candidates and write down why the
others lost — see skills/brand-ui/reference/chart-selection.md.

# StatusBadge  (@elabs-ai/components-ui)
import: import { StatusBadge } from "@elabs-ai/components-ui";
story: https://elabs-ai.com/storybook/?path=/docs/core-statusbadge--docs
purpose: The closed seven-state execution-status vocabulary, each state carrying its own icon as well as its own tone.  [display]
  pairs with: Badge, AgentTimeline, Tool
  avoid next to: Badge
anti-patterns (avoid):
  x Using it for a neutral label or a count — that is Badge; this one asserts an execution state.
  x Inventing an eighth status by passing a custom label into the canonical enum — map an out-of-vocabulary state ONCE, near your domain, through the {label, tone, icon} form.
  x Relying on the tone alone to distinguish two states — the glyph is the second channel that keeps them apart in greyscale.
extends: HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, Omit<VariantProps<typeof statusBadgeVariants>, "status" | "tone">
props (own-declared):
  status: Status | CustomStatus  — The canonical execution status, or a mapped out-of-vocabulary one (#363).
  hideIcon?: boolean  — Render label-only (no status icon).
  appearance?: BadgeAppearance  — Explicit per-instance override of the fill/border/ink treatment — see `Badge`'s own doc. Meaningful only on the colour-bearing statuses (`running`/`complete`/`awaiting-approval`/`failed`) and tones (`info`/`success`/`warning`/`destructive`); `pending`/`denied`/`skipped` and the `neutral` tone are already neutral pills. On a `CustomStatus` (the out-of-vocabulary hatch), `"solid"` is never honoured — the hatch is calm-only (integrity constraint 2, file docblock).
variants (expanded from cva — the real values):
  status: pending | running | complete | awaiting-approval | denied | failed | skipped
  tone: neutral | info | success | warning | destructive
  size: sm | md (default)

# MapCanvas  (@elabs-ai/components-maps)
import: import { MapCanvas } from "@elabs-ai/components-maps";
story: https://elabs-ai.com/storybook/?path=/docs/maps-mapcanvas--docs
purpose: Root MapLibre canvas — theme-aware basemap; the ref is the raw MapLibre Map. With `plan` it is a non-geographic plan instead (a floor, a plant, a carriage) and every layer inside speaks plan units.  [data]
  contains: MapMarker, MapControls, MapClusterLayer, MapGeoJSON, MapRoute, MapPlanImage, MapPlanOverlay
anti-patterns (avoid):
  x Hiding MapLibre's attribution control — the default Carto basemap styles/tiles require it.
  x Importing maplibre-gl CSS in the app — MapCanvas imports its own CSS plus the brand popup overrides.
  x Rendering it in an RSC/SSR path with no client boundary — MapLibre needs WebGL.
  x Mapping plan units into DEGREES to fake a plan coordinate system — degrees are not linear on screen, so a 16:9 plan renders at 2:1. Declare `plan` and let createPlanCrs map into normalized Mercator, where a rectangle stays a rectangle at every zoom.
  x Leaving rotation and pitch on for a plan — a tilted floor plan is unreadable. The `plan` prop turns dragRotate, pitchWithRotate and touchPitch off; do not switch them back on.
  x Combining `plan` with a globe projection — a plan is flat; the projection is ignored with a one-time warning.
extends: Omit<MapLibreGL.MapOptions, "container" | "style" | "interactive">
props (own-declared):
  children?: ReactNode
  className?: string  — Additional CSS classes for the map container.
  theme?: BasemapTheme  — Basemap flavor. If not provided, it is derived from the active brand theme (`data-theme` + that theme's own `color-scheme`), then a `dark`/`light` root class, then the OS preference.
  styles?: { light?: MapStyleOption; dark?: MapStyleOption; }  — Custom map styles for light and dark themes. Overrides the default Carto styles.
  blank?: boolean  — Use a transparent, tile-less basemap instead of the default Carto street basemap — a blank canvas. Used alone it renders nothing; add your own layers on top (`<MapGeoJSON>`, `<MapArc>`, markers, …). Ideal for data visualizations. Ignored when an explicit `styles` prop is provided.
  basemapLabels?: boolean  — Draw the basemap's own place labels. `false` leaves the ground and hides every text label the basemap style carries, so the map's own labels (`MapMarker`'s `label`, `MapAnnotation`) are the only naming on it — the locator recipe, and the default inside `MapInset`, where a full-size label is sliced by the frame. Default `true`.
  projection?: MapProjectionOption  — Map projection: `"mercator"` (MapLibre's default) or `"globe"` for a 3D globe view, or a full MapLibre projection spec. Feature-detected: a MapLibre build that cannot switch projections ignores it (with a console note).
  interactive?: boolean  — `false` makes the map STATIC — the editorial / locator default: no zoom, pan, rotate or keyboard handlers, the default cursor and no tab stop (leave `<MapControls>` out of a static map). Hover and click still reach layers and markers, so tooltips keep working. The viewport can still be set in code (`viewport`, the ref). Default `true`.
  height?: MapResponsive<MapHeight>  — The map's height: CSS px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per tier — `{ base: { aspect: 1.6 }, narrow: { aspect: 1 } }`. Tiers are measured on the map's own width (`narrow` < 480 px, `medium` < 768 px). Unset, the map fills its parent as before; a parent with no height of its own gets `DEFAULT_MAP_HEIGHT` (1.6 : 1, square at `narrow`) instead of 0.
  viewport?: Partial<MapViewport>  — Controlled viewport. When provided together with `onViewportChange`, the map becomes controlled and the viewport is driven by this prop.
  onViewportChange?: (viewport: MapViewport) => void  — Callback fired continuously as the viewport changes (pan, zoom, rotate, pitch). Use standalone to observe changes, or with `viewport` for controlled mode.
  loading?: boolean  — Show a loading overlay on the map (e.g. while the app fetches map data).
  plan?: PlanExtent | PlanCrs  — Turn the canvas into a CUSTOM (non-geographic) plan map: a floor plan, a factory layout, a train carriage, a rack elevation. Pass the plan's extent (`{ width, height }` in the plan's own units) or a `createPlanCrs(…)` result, and every layer inside then speaks PLAN coordinates instead of lng/lat — shapes, routes, markers and popups alike. The plan is fitted on mount, pan and zoom are clamped to its extent, and rotation and pitch are off (a rotated floor plan is unreadable). Pair it with `blank` and, for a picture under the shapes, `<MapPlanImage>`. The plan coordinate system is synthesized on Web Mercator, so it is not a georeference: distances belong to the plan, and a scale bar would lie.
  fitPlan?: boolean  — Fit a plan map to its extent on mount and whenever the extent changes (default: true). Ignored on a geographic map, and skipped when the camera is driven through `viewport`.

args.shape: cohort by month, two categorical axes

content.text:
chart-for "cohort by month, two categorical axes" — 5 candidate(s), ranked:
  read as: time × category
  1. DumbbellChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 3)
     shape: two time points per category — a before and after, or a range with two ends
     avoid when: more than 2 points per category — use small-multiple lines
  2. HeatmapChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 2.25)
     shape: two categorical axes (weekday by hour, for example) with one numeric value per cell — ticket volume, event counts; many small cells favour mode="dot" over the default cell fill
     avoid when: more than about 10 columns of continuous data, or exact cell values matter more than the pattern
  3. BumpChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 1.5)
     shape: rank of several entities over ordered periods
     avoid when: only 2 periods — use a dumbbell chart
  4. LiveLineChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 1)
     shape: a metric updating in real time, appended over a rolling window
     avoid when: the series is static or historical — use a line chart
  5. LineChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts, score 1)
     shape: one or more measures over continuous time, where the trend itself is the point
     avoid when: many overlapping series (more than about 6) — use small multiples (ChartMultiples), a stream area chart or a composed chart

Per the chart-selection rules: compare at least 3 candidates and write down why the
others lost — see skills/brand-ui/reference/chart-selection.md.

# HeatmapChart  (@elabs-ai/components-charts)
import: import { HeatmapChart } from "@elabs-ai/components-charts";
story: https://elabs-ai.com/storybook/?path=/docs/charts-heatmapchart--docs
purpose: Two discrete dimensions × one value — weekday × hour, product × region, or a year of days.  [chart]
  used inside: ChartFrame, ChartCard
  pairs with: ChartTooltip
anti-patterns (avoid):
  x steps: 0 (the continuous ramp) when the reader must compare exact values — opacity is not countable; keep the stepped ramp or turn showValues on.
  x emptyValue="blank" on data that contains real zeroes — a measured zero then looks identical to a missing row, which is the one thing the pinprick exists to prevent.
  x Forcing the calendar variant into a narrow box (overflow-hidden, a tall aspectRatio) — it enforces a minimum width and scrolls on purpose; squeezed day cells fall below the 24px target size.
  x Leaning on the darkest ramp step to say "this is the peak" — colour alone; highlight draws the ring, and a diverging palette needs showValues or its negative hatch for sign.
extends: ChartSelectionProps, ChartInteractionProps, ChartSelectionGestureProps, ChartCategoryNavigatorProps
props (own-declared):
  data: Record<string, unknown>[]  — One row per cell. Rows the grid has no place for are ignored.
  x: string  — Row key holding the COLUMN value (discrete; an ISO date in the calendar variant).
  y: string  — Row key holding the ROW value (discrete). Ignored by `variant="calendar"`.
  valueKey: string  — Row key holding the number. A non-finite or missing value is an empty cell.
  mode?: HeatmapMode  — How a cell encodes its value. - `"cell"` — a filled square whose SHADE is the value (L16, G20). - `"dot"` — a dot whose AREA is the value (F10, L4, L17); the shade still tracks the ramp, so the two encodings are redundant, not rival. Default: `"cell"` for `variant="matrix"`, `"dot"` for `variant="calendar"`.
  variant?: HeatmapVariant  — Which grid the cells land on. `"calendar"` reads `x` as an ISO date, lays the days out as 7 weekday rows × one column per ISO week, ticks the first Monday of each month, and ignores `y` entirely.
  palette?: HeatmapPalette  — Which ordered ramp the values are drawn from. Default `"sequential"`.
  steps?: number  — How many countable ramp steps. Default {@link DEFAULT_HEATMAP_STEPS}. `0` asks for a continuous ramp — one hue at a continuously varying opacity, because the ramp entries are `var()` references nothing can interpolate.
  showValues?: boolean  — Print each cell's value on it, as halo text (G20). Default `false`, except on `palette="diverging"` where it defaults to `true` — see decision 3 in the module docblock for why sign cannot ride on hue alone.
  highlight?: HeatmapHighlight  — Which cell gets the dashed peak ring. Default `"max"`, the lieflat convention; the ringed cell is also the one the accessible summary names.
  rowHighlight?: (rowLabel: string) => boolean  — Every row this predicate matches (by its \`y\` label) gets a dashed rail around the whole row plus a bold row label -- emphasis for "the finding is about this ROW", not just one cell in it (#280). Shape + weight, never hue alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Default \`undefined\` -- no row emphasis.
  showValueHalo?: boolean  — Halo behind a \`mode="cell"\` value label. Default \`true\`. A flat filled plate already carries its own on-mark ink pair (#238); set \`false\` when that alone reads clean and a halo would ring-fringe a mid-tone fill (#280) -- never needed for \`mode="dot"\`, where the label sits on the busier plot ground.
  emptyMarkScale?: number  — Side of the no-data outline, as a fraction of the cell's shorter side. Default {@link DEFAULT_EMPTY_MARK_SCALE}. Shrink it for a denser grid or a deliberately quieter empty state (#280); the legend's swatch is a KEY at its own fixed size and does not scale with this.
  emptyValue?: HeatmapEmptyValue  — What a cell with nothing to shade draws. `"quiet"` (default) keeps the two facts apart: a measured `0` is the 0.9px pinprick (measured, and the answer was nothing), a `null` is a hairline outline of the empty cell (never measured). Each gets its own legend key, shown only when the grid holds one. `"blank"` draws neither.
  xOrder?: string[]  — Column order. Defaults to first-seen order in `data`.
  yOrder?: string[]  — Row order. Defaults to first-seen order in `data`.
  cellRadius?: number  — Corner radius of a `mode="cell"` square, in px. Default 4 (L16).
  valueFormat?: ChartValueFormat  — How values are rendered in labels, the tooltip and the legend. Default `"compact"`.
  showLegend?: boolean  — Show the ramp key below the plot. Default `true`.
  legendLabels?: "endpoints" | "ranges"  — How the legend key states the scale — the same `"ranges"`/`"endpoints"` vocabulary `RampLegend`'s `scale.labels` uses (RM-118). `"endpoints"` (default, unchanged): `lo`/`hi` bracket the strip. `"ranges"`: one `from–to` label under every swatch, so a reader can place a cell in its step without hovering it — most useful together with a small `steps`.
  xAxisLabel?: string  — A visible title for the column axis (#280), e.g. "Months since signup" — printed directly under the plot, ABOVE the legend, so it reads as the axis's own caption rather than a floating sentence after the key. Default `undefined` (no title printed). Not a substitute for `accessibleLabel`/ `accessibleDescription`, which already state the axis in prose for AT.
  margin?: Partial<HeatmapMargin>  — Plot-area insets. Merged over the variant's own defaults.
  aspectRatio?: string  — Aspect ratio of the plot body. Default `"16 / 9"` (`"6 / 1"` for calendar).
  plotHeight?: Responsive<ChartPlotHeight>  — The plot's own height (ADR 0039): px, or `{ aspect }` (width ÷ height), optionally per breakpoint.
  revealOn?: ChartRevealOn  — When the enter stagger plays (RM-020). `"mount"` (default) plays as soon as the chart renders; `"inView"` holds every cell hidden until the plot scrolls into view, then plays once.
  loading?: boolean  — Layout-shaped skeleton instead of the data.
  emptyMessage?: string  — Supporting sentence of the empty state, shown when there is nothing to plot.
  emptyTitle?: string  — Title of the empty state. Default `"No data"`.
  emptyAction?: ReactNode  — An action for the empty state — typically the control that undoes the filter which emptied the grid. Rendered below the message.
  accessibleLabel?: ChartA11yProps["accessibleLabel"]  — Accessible name for the chart region. Defaults to a generated summary ("Heatmap, 7 rows × 24 columns, peak 42 at Wed 14:00.") — passing one both overrides it and is how the sentence gets localized.
  accessibleDescription?: ChartA11yProps["accessibleDescription"]  — Supplemental description read after the label.
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
  scrollbar?: ChartCategoryNavigatorProps["scrollbar"]  — Overview strip style. Default `"none"`. `"miniChart"` / `"bar"` / `"auto"` mount it once the categories overflow `maxVisibleItems`.
  maxVisibleItems?: ChartCategoryNavigatorProps["maxVisibleItems"]  — Categories the plot shows at once while scrolling (the strip's window). Default `"auto"`.
  selectionGestures?: ChartSelectionGestureProps["selectionGestures"]  — Gestures to enable: `"range"` on an axis, `"rect"` / `"lasso"` on marks. Needs `onSelectionIntent`; unset, there is no gesture layer.
  onSelectionIntent?: ChartSelectionGestureProps["onSelectionIntent"]  — Receives one `ChartSelectionIntent` (`field`, `values`, `mode`) per gesture — per ✓ in `explicit`.
  selectionConfirm?: ChartSelectionGestureProps["selectionConfirm"]  — `"immediate"` (default) or `"explicit"`: provisional paint, ✓ / Enter commit, ✕ / Esc cancel.
